sources.title: UNESCO, Barkcloth making in Uganda
sources.note: Craft description: Mutuba inner bark, wooden mallets, shaded working area, household and ceremonial uses, Ngonge craftspeople and nineteenth-century cotton competition.

sources.title: Buganda Kingdom, The Great Lukiiko
sources.note: Historical Origins; Composition and Structure; Notable Developments. The institution's own account is used for its council and cultural role, not its promotional claims of age or democracy.

sources.title: Nyege Nyege Tapes, Buganda Royal Music Revival (2021)
sources.note: About, track list and recording credits. Credits identify sessions in 1947, 1949, 1950, 1952, 1967, 1988 and 2017; they are more precise than the introductory date range. No song lyrics are reproduced.

sources.title: UNESCO, Uganda launches new initiatives for Kasubi Tombs and Rwenzori Mountains (8 September 2026)
sources.note: Kasubi paragraphs: restoration after the 2010 fire, removal from the danger list in 2023 and new conservation work in 2026. The proposed gallery is not treated as an existing museum.

sources.title: Republic of Uganda, Constitution of 1967, article 118
sources.note: Government Printer edition, preamble dated 8 September 1967 and printed page 72 (PDF page 82), article 118(1)-(2). General abolition in 1967 was given retrospective effect from 24 May 1966 specifically for Buganda. Used as a historical document.

sources.title: Graham Connah, The salt of Bunyoro: seeking the origins of an African Kingdom (1991)
sources.note: Public Extract, Antiquity 65, pages 479-494: early second-millennium origins of an economic center and carved-roulette pottery. The 2015 online publication date is distinct from the 1991 article date. Full paywalled text has not been represented as read.

sources.title: Uganda Ministry of Tourism, Wildlife and Antiquities, Kibiro Salt Producing Village (2025)
sources.note: Tentative List submission of 30 January 2025, Description and Justification: women's work, garden rights, recycled earth, capillary action, leaching, boiling and pottery. Internally inconsistent claims of 800 or 900 years and 1400 AD are not used. Tentative listing is not World Heritage inscription.

sources.title: UNESCO, Empaako tradition of western Uganda
sources.note: 2013 inscription description: shared names, social ties, household naming ceremony, aunts, clan head, millet and smoked beef, tree planting and transmission concerns. A documented practice, not a claim that every household follows an identical ritual.

sources.title: Treccani, Bunyoro, Dizionario di Storia (2010)
sources.note: Second paragraph: defeat and deportation of Kabarega by a British-Buganda coalition in 1899; colonial incorporation and territorial loss; cultural restoration and Iguru I in 1994. Its generalized 1966 abolition date is corrected with article 118 of the original 1967 constitution.

sources.title: G. N. Uzoigwe, Bunyoro-Kitara Revisited (2013)
sources.note: Public abstract, first online 2012 and journal volume 48(1), 2013: an explicitly attributed interpretation involving rulers' decisions, human and animal disease, conquest and territorial loss. Numerical loss estimates and priority claims are not repeated.

sources.title: Uganda Electoral Commission, History of Elections in Uganda
sources.note: 1964 referendum section: Buyaga and Bugangaizi, colonial transfer in 1894-95 and voters' decision to return to Bunyoro. Generalized crisis chronology is checked against the original constitution.

proposedOverrides.summary: Buganda's history joins royal councils with barkcloth, Kasubi's plant-based architecture and generations of musicians. Its restored royal institution has a cultural role in Uganda; Baganda communities continue.

proposedOverrides.summary: Bunyoro's history includes Kibiro's salt gardens and pottery, regional exchange and Empaako naming. Colonial conquest, abolition of kingship and its cultural restoration changed institutions while Banyoro communities continued.
